chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The persons most attached to the prophets are those who know most what the prophets have brought,
Then he (peace be upon him) recited:
(“Verily, of men the nearest to Abraham are surely those who followed him and this (Our) Prophet (Muḥammad) and those who believe.”)

Then he (peace be upon him) said: The friend of Muḥammad is he who obeys Allāh, even though he may have no blood relationship, and the enemy of Muḥammad is he who disobeys Allāh even though he may have near kinship!
ai.seo_question: How is proximity to the prophets defined in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that true proximity to the prophets is defined by adherence to their teachings and obedience to God, rather than mere genealogical lineage. By citing Surah Ali 'Imran, he illustrates that just as followers of Abraham are his true kin, so too are those who obey God the true relatives of Muhammad, a concept central to the Shia understanding of Walayah. This distinction elevates spiritual and practical obedience above tribal or familial bonds, reinforcing the idea that the 'Ahl al-Bayt' and the faithful are connected through divine command.
